subject: TTL sunset sequencing & final confirmation checklist for prompt-output/log retention
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@curedx.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: TTL-driven retention sunset + confirmation for CureDx prompts/logs

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. CureDx is preparing for a scheduled data residency audit and we need a clear, auditable flow for TTL-driven retention sunsets covering: prompt inputs, model outputs, and inference logs (KV cache traces, request metadata). Specifically:

- A sequential timeline for the purge (what runs first / dependent artifacts);
- Evidence we can share with auditors (manifest + checksums);
- Customer-facing confirmation emails templates (so our security/compliance team accepts them).

Can Redwood provide a single-run orchestration plan (we prefer a one-window execution) and an example of the final confirmation email + attachments? We also need an estimate of how long the sweep takes for our account (approx 240M tokens/month, US region).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our audit kickoff is Monday.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Security Operations
CureDx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@curedx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: TTL-driven retention sunset + confirmation for CureDx prompts/logs

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and the timeline. High-level plan attached (redwood-ops-ttl-sunset-runbook-v1.pdf). Below is the sequencing we propose for a single-window execution and the artifacts you'll receive post-sweep.

Execution sequence (single window):
1) Read-only verification pass (0-15m): inventory of keys, prompt-output pointers, and log partitions to build the manifest.
2) KV prefix eviction (15-45m): remove cached prefixes aligned to TTL; quick eviction to minimize live latency interaction.
3) Prompt-output deletion (45-90m): remove object-store blobs and their index entries; uses batch deletes and tombstone markers.
4) Inference log purge (90-120m): scrub request traces, rotate logs, and apply irreversible delete operations.
5) Post-run verification (120-150m): compute manifest, SHA256 of manifest, and run logchain integrity checks.

Expected duration: for your volume (~240M tokens/mo) we estimate 2–2.5 hours total with a 95th percentile bound of 3 hours if batching consolidates poorly. We will provide: sweep-manifest-YYYYMMDD.csv, logchain-sha256-YYYYMMDD.txt, and an audit-ready email with attachments.

Attachments: redwood-ops-ttl-sunset-runbook-v1.pdf [attachment: redwood-ops-ttl-sunset-runbook-v1.pdf].
DocuSign: we can issue a confirmation DocuSign envelope for CureDx approval; link included after you ACK.

Next steps:
- Please confirm a preferred 3-hour maintenance window (we prefer 22:00–01:00 PST to minimize traffic).
- Approve the runbook as-is or flag any required additional controls.

If OK, we'll schedule the run and loop in the execution team (Ben) for pre-checks.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: TTL-driven retention sunset + confirmation for CureDx prompts/logs

Kimberly / Marissa — quick checklist from ops side before we lock the window:
- Pre-run: snapshot index + temp manifest export to internal S3 (readonly, tagged) — 30m.
- Execution: throttle-bucket size 1000 qps ceiling, background deletes with backoff.
- Fallback: automatic pause & rollback to tombstone-only state if 5xx rate > 0.5% for >5m.
- Post-run: generate CSV manifest, compute SHA256 (logchain-sha256-20260418.txt), and store both to the secure evidence bucket.

I can own the run and coordinate the RBAC task token; will need Marissa to confirm customer communication language for the final email.

Ben
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
